cards.front: Recall a key point about Marriage, Divorce & Demography
cards.back: Marriage patterns: the marriage rate in the UK has fallen to its lowest level since records began. First marriages have declined; the average age of first marriage has risen (30 for women, 32 for men). Reasons: secularisation (less religious pressure), changing attitudes (cohabitation is now socially acceptable), women's economic independence (no longer need to marry for financial security).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Marriage, Divorce & Demography
cards.back: Divorce: the divorce rate increased dramatically after the 1969 Divorce Reform Act (made 'irretrievable breakdown' sufficient grounds). Currently about 42% of marriages end in divorce. Reasons: easier divorce laws, less stigma, women's financial independence, rising expectations of marriage (Giddens: confluent love - relationships only survive while both partners are satisfied).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Marriage, Divorce & Demography
cards.back: Cohabitation: living together without marriage. Has increased significantly - 20% of couples now cohabit. Some see it as a trial marriage; others see it as an alternative to marriage. Cohabiting couples have fewer legal rights than married couples. About half of cohabitations lead to marriage.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Marriage, Divorce & Demography
cards.back: Birth rates: UK total fertility rate is about 1.6 children per woman (below replacement level of 2.1). Reasons: contraception, women's careers, later marriage, cost of raising children, changing values. Death rates: have fallen due to medical advances, better nutrition, improved sanitation. Life expectancy: 81 years (UK average).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Marriage, Divorce & Demography
cards.back: Ageing population: the proportion of people over 65 is increasing (currently 19% in the UK). Causes: falling birth rates, longer life expectancy. Implications: increased pension and healthcare costs, a smaller working-age population supporting more dependants, but also positive contributions (grandparents providing childcare, voluntary work).

cards.front: What should you know about sociology exam tips?
cards.back: When discussing demographic trends, always use specific statistics (divorce rate, fertility rate, life expectancy) and explain the social causes AND consequences of changes. Link to perspectives for evaluation.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: The increase in divorce shows that families are breaking down and society is in decline.
